text:
Gray but quiet midday, and that's how the day stays. The leftover snow showers wrapped up this morning, and we're dry under a lid of cloud. We started in the mid 30s and should creep to about 41 this afternoon, with a light north breeze that makes it feel colder than it is. Tonight stays cloudy and drops to around 29. A few snow showers could sneak in after 5am, but nothing that matters.

Saturday is the wetter day. The morning looks like the best window for errands or a walk. Showers fill in around late morning and get steadier by afternoon, peaking in the evening and lasting into the night. It's a mix of rain and wet snow, with graupel possible, and we climb to about 42. Because the air is a bit unstable, the showers will be spotty and heavy at times, so you may get soaked, then see a break. Expect only a trace of snow on the grass at most, and a very light total of rain, around a twentieth of an inch. The European model is the wettest of the bunch, but the amounts stay small either way.

Sunday starts with a few snow showers before 8, then a rain and snow mix until about 1 as things taper off. We stay mostly cloudy with a high near 42. It should be done by evening.

Next week turns dry, with sunshine Monday and highs warming toward the mid 50s by midweek. Keep the umbrella and a hat handy Saturday, and save outdoor plans for Saturday morning or Sunday afternoon.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-13T14:45:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Widespread upslope snow showers Saturday, gradually tapering off Sunday.

AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 944 AM EST Friday... The Winter Weather Advisory has expired as the heaviest snow has ended across the Advisory areas.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: For the weekend, cyclonic northwest flow will prevail under an upper level low. However, for today, the region will be in an area of subsidence between shortwaves so it will be mostly dry, though a couple upslope flurries will be possible in the mountains. A potent embedded shortwave will pass south tomorrow and tomorrow night, bringing widespread showers. While they will be most concentrated in the typical northwest flow upslope areas, very marginal instability will develop in the lower 10,000 ft in the atmosphere due to cold air aloft and solar heating. This will cause the precipitation to trend more convective, especially Saturday afternoon. Therefore, snow showers will be able to survive crossing the terrain and should pass through the downslope areas like the Connecticut River Valley, though likely in a lighter form. While temperatures will rise above freezing below 2,000 ft, and likely reach 40 in the lowest points, temperatures will drop significantly in any of the showers. Therefore, even though consistent snow levels will likely only be down to around 1,000-1,500 ft, a period of graupel or even brief wet snow will be possible all the way down into the valleys. However, any continuous accumulations should generally be limited to above 2,000 ft. The showers will gradually become less and less widespread heading into Sunday, and they should be done by Sunday evening. Accumulations by the end should be in the 1-4 inch range above 2,500 ft, with mostly brief coatings that melt below that. The lowest accumulating snow will fall Saturday night. Moisture off Lake Champlain will enhance the showers in the parts of the Champlain Valley and Greens, but the more convective nature may prevent the formation of distinct bands. KEY MESSAGE 2: Deterministic and ensemble guidance are in strong agreement that an 2-3 standard deviation ridge of high pressure will be centered to the south and west of the North Country next week. Temperatures will start seasonably mild with highs in the 40s on Friday with temperatures warming a few degrees each day. Highs by Friday will warm into the mid 50s which will be 3-7 degrees above normal. Some of the deterministic guidance is trying to flatten the ridge on Friday with a strong shortwave but the likelihood of this scenario seems pretty low considering just how strong and amplified the upper level ridge is forecasted to be. Should the ridge break down, then it's possible we see some rain chances Friday into next weekend but again that's a very low confidence scenario as dry weather seems the most likely case at this time.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Friday! Any leftover snow showers across central and southern parts of the area are quickly wrapping up through the mid to late morning. We are left dry, but cloudy through the rest of the day ahead. Temperatures for the day will head back into the upper 30s and lower 40s by this afternoon. Tonight mainly cloudy skies stick around as overnight lows fall into the 30s. This weekend stays gray, cloudy, and a bit unsettled. Clouds stay pretty stubborn as we continue to see valley rain showers and mountain snow showers. This time it will be the mountains of the northern half of the area that seem to be the big winner. Through Saturday and Sunday the mountain peaks north could run upwards of 6″ of new snow. Just like the last system, this will be highly elevation dependent, and as you get below the summits the snow totals drop off very quickly. I am not anticipating many issues on the roads, but some of the mountain passes could become slick from time to time. Temperatures both days are generally in the upper 30s to the lower 40s. We flip a switch into next week as sunshine tries to start to make an appearance into the day Monday. Temperatures are still on the cooler side to start the week in the low to mid 40s. Sunshine continues through Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of next week. With all the sunshine we’ll see temperatures head back towards the low and mid 50s by midweek.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-13T00:00:00Z — same caveat): Slippery travel early in southern Vermont, cloudy Friday afternoon — Rain and elevation snow will wrap up Friday morning. Some roads will be slippery, either from frozen standing water, or snow accumulation. Mountain towns will experience more of this. Little to no precipitation is expected north of Burlington through Friday morning. Several inches of snow will fall in southern parts of the region, higher up. The weekend brings more clouds with persistent rain and snow showers. Snow accumulation is expected in the northern mountains over the weekend. Drier and brighter weather is likely next week, followed by a warmup into the 50s.
